title: watchdog-harness-keep-build
desc: BUILD-PLAN: Add harness:keep reap-protect + kill-audit to wkdoctor.ps1 EmergencyKill (lines 83-139). Apply in a fresh low-pace session via Haiku agent.
steps: SCOPE: Target = D:/GitHub/wkappbot-sdk/bin/wkdoctor.ps1 lines 83-139 (EmergencyKill block). Guard invocation point = wkharness-guards.ps1:789 via wkdoctor.cmd. This plan adds 3 new helper functions (Get-EkCmdLine, Get-EkAncestry, Get-HarnessKeepPatterns), initializes 3 vars (keepPatterns/auditDir/auditPath) before the kill loop, modifies the loop body to honor harness:keep patterns, and writes kill-audit entries to JSONL. All edits are INSIDE the if (EmergencyKill) block. Prerequisite skill reads: wkdoctor-sdk-environment-health-check + wkharness-guards + claude-md-harness-rules.

NEW FUNCTION Get-EkCmdLine: Insert as a new function after the closing brace of Get-RamPct (after line 89). Signature: function Get-EkCmdLine { param([int]Pid) }. Body: try { (Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter ProcessId=Pid -ErrorAction Stop).CommandLine } catch { return empty-string }. Returns the full CommandLine string for the given PID via CIM Win32_Process.CommandLine, or empty string on any CIM error. Reuses the same CIM query pattern already used in Build-SafePool at line 98.

NEW FUNCTION Get-EkAncestry: Insert after Get-EkCmdLine closing brace. Signature: function Get-EkAncestry { param([int]Pid) }. Init chain as List[PSCustomObject] and seen as HashSet[int]. Set cur=Pid. Loop: while cur-gt-0 and seen.Add(cur) -- query CIM Win32_Process for ProcessId=cur; if found append PSCustomObject(pid=ProcessId,name=Name,cmdline=CommandLine) to chain and set cur=ParentProcessId; break on CIM error. Return @(chain). Produces an array of {pid,name,cmdline} from target process up to root, using the same parent-chain walk as wkharness-agent-name.ps1.

NEW FUNCTION Get-HarnessKeepPatterns: Insert after Get-EkAncestry closing brace. No params. Init patterns as List[string]. For each file path in (Join-Path PWD CLAUDE.md) and (Join-Path env:USERPROFILE .claude CLAUDE.md): if Test-Path file then Get-Content, foreach line match regex ^## harness:keep (.+) at line start, Add Matches[1].Trim() to list. Return @(patterns). Implements the same CLAUDE.md rule loader as the other harness directives (safe/block/warn/skill). See skill claude-md-harness-rules for rule syntax.

INIT VARS: After the Build-SafePool return @() line (line 112) and before the dollar-killed=0 line (line 114), insert: keepPatterns = Get-HarnessKeepPatterns; auditDir = Join-Path env:USERPROFILE .claude/wkharness; auditPath = Join-Path auditDir emergency-kill-audit.jsonl; if not Test-Path auditDir then New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path auditDir -Force then pipe to Out-Null.

MODIFY KILL LOOP BODY: Replace the inner try-catch block (lines 120-125 OLD) inside foreach (proc in pool). NEW body order: (1) cmdline = Get-EkCmdLine proc.Id. (2) kept=false; foreach pat in keepPatterns: if proc.Name -match pat OR cmdline -match pat then set kept=true and break. (3) If kept AND ram-lt-85: Write-Host [ek] KEPT proc.Name pid=N ws=MB ram=% harness:keep match warn-only in Cyan; then continue (skip kill). (4) ancestry = Get-EkAncestry proc.Id. (5) try block: call wkappbot taskkill force proc.Id pipe to Out-Null; killed++; wsMb=int(proc.WS/1MB); shortCmd = cmdline clamped at 80 chars with ellipsis; Write-Host [ek] killed proc.Name pid=N ws=MB ram=% cmd=[shortCmd] in Yellow; serialize auditLine as PSCustomObject{ts,pid,name,ws_mb,ram_pct,reason,full_cmdline,ancestry} via ConvertTo-Json -Compress -Depth 4; Add-Content auditPath auditLine -Encoding UTF8. reason field = keep-override-ge85pct when kept is true else safe-pool-reap. (6) catch {}.

SELFTEST PLAN: Verify the 3 helpers and the keep-guard branch without touching live processes. (a) Call Get-EkCmdLine with PID of current process (dollar-pid): assert non-empty string returned. (b) Call Get-EkAncestry with current PID: assert returned array has at least 1 item and each item has pid/name/cmdline properties. (c) Write a temp file Temp-CLAUDE.md with single line '## harness:keep keeptest-marker', temporarily set PWD to Temp, call Get-HarnessKeepPatterns: assert 'keeptest-marker' appears in result. (d) Build a synthetic pool PSObject with Name=keeptest-marker and WS=1MB; simulate ram=70 (lt 85); run the new loop body logic: assert kept=true, assert Write-Host KEPT fires, assert continue path prevents kill. (e) After real edit lands in a live session, run wkdoctor -EmergencyKill from a temp CWD and verify emergency-kill-audit.jsonl exists at USERPROFILE/.claude/wkharness/ (0 entries is fine if RAM is below threshold).

VERIFY SYNTAX: After applying all edits, run the PowerShell Parser check inline: assign errors as array of ParseError; call [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile with path D:/GitHub/wkappbot-sdk/bin/wkdoctor.ps1 and ref-null/ref-errors args; if errors.Count equals 0 print SYNTAX OK else print SYNTAX ERRORS colon count. Expected output: SYNTAX OK. Do NOT commit until SYNTAX OK is confirmed. Mirrors the existing selftest pattern in wkharness-status.ps1.

BOUNDARY-CHATTER HYSTERESIS (user 2026-06-04): also add deadband so the emergency-kill stops re-firing on every tool call at the 60 percent line. Per memory/watchdog-harness-keep-spec.md: keep TRIGGER at 60 percent, but after a fire that exhausts the safe pool apply a COOLDOWN (no re-fire for N seconds) plus a higher RE-ARM threshold (only re-fire if RAM climbs above about 67 percent). Reap only as low as the SAFE pool allows (do NOT chase a fixed 30 percent target -- Memory Compression and chrome are not safely killable). When the safe pool is exhausted and RAM is still high, WARN that reaping cannot fix it and point to the Defender dev-folder exclusions (the root cure). Track the last-fire timestamp + re-arm mark in the guards.ps1 hook trigger (operational ts like the pace cache).

REAP-PRIORITY ORDER (user directive 2026-06-05, MANDATORY): AI processes AND their descendant process trees are the LOWEST reap priority. They are killed LAST and only as an absolute last resort at true OOM (the 85 percent hard override). The emergency-kill pool MUST reap EXTERNAL or unknown hogs FIRST (WmiPrvSE, Defender MsMpEng spawn storm, orphaned non-AI processes), then respawnable hosts, and touch the AI work tree only if RAM is still critical after exhausting those. Definition of AI process to spare: claude.exe, wkappbot-core, wkchat, wka11y, codex, plus any python or pythonw or node spawned by an AI session within roughly the last hour, AND their CHILD processes (walk the process tree, do not merely name-match). This generalizes the blunt name-based harness:keep into a proper tree-aware soft-priority sort in Build-SafePool. LIVE 2026-06-05: the watchdog already KEEPS python node codex by name (warn-only) and kills only external WmiPrvSE, so the principle is half-working; this step mandates the FULL tree (descendants plus claude.exe plus the 1h-spawn window) be last-priority, not just the named set. Never preferentially kill the AI's own running work to free RAM -- the culprit is almost always external.

SELF-SPARE THE REAPER -- INVARIANT #0 (user 2026-06-05, the doctor-kills-itself paradox): wkdoctor.ps1 IS the emergency-kill tool, so it MUST hard-EXCLUDE from the kill pool entirely (never a candidate, evaluated FIRST, above even the AI-tree last-priority tier): (a) its own process -- the PowerShell running wkdoctor -EmergencyKill; (b) its entire descendant process tree spawned during the reap; (c) the invoking PreToolUse hook process chain up to the live AI session that triggered it. A reaper that kills itself or its own children mid-reap is broken. WMI CAVEAT: Windows spawns WmiPrvSE via DCOM to service wkdoctor's OWN Get-CimInstance / process-enumeration queries; WmiPrvSE parent is WinMgmt/svchost (not a direct child of wkdoctor) so it cannot be attributed by simple parent-walk -- be cautious: do NOT blanket-reap every WmiPrvSE during the run (that can kill the very provider servicing the enumeration and break it); prefer reaping only WmiPrvSE that are clearly the external storm (high count, aged, not just-spawned this tick). Ordering: invariant #0 self-spare -> AI-tree last-priority -> external/unknown hogs reaped first among candidates. Self-preservation of the reaper comes before everything.

CLAUDE.md RESOLUTION GAP (verified 2026-06-05 from wkappbot-sdk/bin/wkdoctor.ps1 Get-HarnessKeepPatterns L117-126): the reaper reads harness:keep from ONLY two files -- (1) Join-Path PWD CLAUDE.md (the wkdoctor INVOKER current working directory = the triggering AI session repo) and (2) the global USERPROFILE .claude CLAUDE.md. It does NOT resolve the repo-root CLAUDE.md of each TARGET process being considered for kill. CONSEQUENCE: when the watchdog fires from a session in repo A, a kill-candidate process belonging to repo B is matched only against repo-A plus global keep patterns; repo-B own per-repo harness:keep is IGNORED. Same class as harness-skill-guard-cross-repo. Also the PWD-dependence means a cron-invoked reaper with CWD=. reads the wrong project CLAUDE.md. So today the GLOBAL harness:keep is the only reliably-applied layer (read on every invocation regardless of trigger CWD) -- which is why broadening the GLOBAL keep set is both safe and necessary as the universal floor, and why a project-only keep edit is honored only when CWD matches that repo. PROPER FIX: for each kill candidate, resolve ITS process working directory up to the nearest repo-root CLAUDE.md and union that repo harness:keep with global, so each repo can declare narrow per-repo keep rules that apply no matter which session triggers the reaper -- then the broad global set can be narrowed back to unambiguous AI-infra names. Pairs with the reaper self-spare invariant #0 and the AI-tree last-priority steps.

PROCESS-ENUMERATION VIA wkappbot-core IPC, NOT WMI (user design 2026-06-05, ROOT-CURE for the WmiPrvSE storm): wkdoctor currently enumerates processes with Get-CimInstance (WMI) to obtain cmdline+parent for classification -- but WMI makes Windows spawn WmiPrvSE provider processes, and under load that IS the storm the watchdog is fighting (and ironically the reaper own WMI queries spawn the WmiPrvSE it then must spare -- the invariant #0 WMI caveat). DESIGN: instead, wkdoctor MIMICS THE LAUNCHER (connects to the wkappbot-core named pipe) and IPC-requests process enumeration from wkappbot-core, which finds processes via NATIVE Win32 (toolhelp snapshot / NtQuerySystemInformation / its a11y-find layer) -- NO WMI, so ZERO WmiPrvSE spawned. This UNIFIES every Windows process-query in the harness into ONE wkappbot-core IPC channel instead of N independent WMI consumers (each session/tool spawning its own provider). PAYOFF: kills the WmiPrvSE storm at the root (the RAM/CPU spikes, the background-agent output-capture failures, the per-call watchdog churn all trace to it), removes the reaper-self-WMI paradox, and yields richer data (cmdline+parent) than Get-Process without the WMI cost. CAVEAT/FALLBACK: if wkappbot-core is itself down or throttled, fall back to Get-Process (native, no WMI, but no cmdline) rather than WMI. Pairs with -DefenderFix (stops Defender scanning) -- together they target the two storm sources. Worth a FEAT suggest to wkappbot-core to expose a process-enumeration IPC verb that wkdoctor and any harness tool can call.
